# Financial methods verification addendum

Checked October 18, 2026 against the financial section of `site/research/competitive-services-review-2026-10-18.md`, current public primary sources and retained runtime files. Research only: no app changes, accounts, payments or student data.

The synthesis is correct that the generic experience-year amounts are scenarios. **TWC's entry/experienced statistics cannot validate exact five-, ten- or twenty-year salaries.** One concrete saved/live-source discrepancy also needs review: the runtime uses $66,019 for Austin Fire post-academy entry, while its currently published official page says $67,999. The page does not date that salary change, so this does not establish when the older amount ceased to apply.

## TWC and OEWS definitions

TWC defines **entry wage as the mean wage of the lowest-paid third** of workers in the selected occupation/location; **experienced wage is the mean of the upper-paid two-thirds**. These are subgroup averages, not the 33rd/67th percentile boundaries, measured tenure bands or observations after twenty years. A worker's career cannot be reconstructed by moving between these cross-sectional averages. The main synthesis's limitation is supported; link directly to the definitions rather than the TWC homepage. [TWC TexasWages About and FAQ](https://texaswages.com/Home/About).

BLS OEWS covers wage/salary jobs and excludes self-employed workers, owners/partners of unincorporated firms, household workers and unpaid family workers. Wages are straight-time gross pay: tips, commissions and production incentives can be included; overtime premiums, stock bonuses, nonproduction bonuses and employer-paid benefits are excluded. A percentile is a boundary in the wage distribution, not an experience group. The survey does not gather demographic information; neither a median nor a lower percentile is a measured first-year salary. [OEWS FAQ, sections C and D](https://www.bls.gov/oes/oes_ques.htm).

Consequences for interpretation: “employee earnings” is safer than “what a business owner makes”; revenue, profit and employee wages are different quantities. Excluding benefits does not mean subtracting the employer's entire health-insurance cost from these wages. Compare the same annual-hours assumptions, and use a source's actual annual contract amount when it differs from a generic hourly annualization. These are methodological implications, not additional OEWS fields.

## Which sources can support experience claims

| Source | What it actually measures | Appropriate role and limits |
|---|---|---|
| **BLS NLSY longitudinal histories** | Repeated observations of the same people, with job dates, earnings and work histories. | Genuine longitudinal research material exists, but BLS explicitly says NLS is **not suited to occupation/industry wage estimates** and cannot produce representative state, county or metro estimates. It does not supply a ready-made current Austin salary curve for each career. [NLS FAQ](https://www.bls.gov/nls/questions-and-answers.htm), [employment/work-history documentation](https://nlsinfo.org/content/cohorts/nlsy79/topical-guide/employment/introduction). |
| **BLS Modeled Wage Estimates (MWE)** | Occupational/local hourly pay grouped by job characteristics; work levels use knowledge, controls/complexity, contacts and physical environment. | Useful **historical role-level benchmark**, not measured experience years. Importantly, the program is **discontinued**: final publication August 2024, covering 2023 estimates. Do not propose MWE as a maintained current wage feed. [Discontinuation announcement](https://www.bls.gov/mwe/), [work-level methodology](https://www.bls.gov/mwe/factsheets/grouped-work-levels-factsheet.htm). |
| **NCSES National Survey of College Graduates** | Repeated cross-sectional information on college graduates, occupations, salaries and degree histories. “Years since highest degree” is survey year minus degree year. | Can contextualize graduate outcomes. Years since degree is not actual years in an occupation; published full-time salaries are not automatically calendar-year adjusted for educational employees. Not a general all-career Austin tenure series. [2023 NSCG definitions and tables](https://www.ncses.nsf.gov/surveys/national-survey-college-graduates/2023). |
| **Census PSEO** | Linked graduate earnings at **one, five and ten years after graduation**, by participating institution, degree, field and cohort. | A real elapsed-time outcome for education-route comparisons; not years of occupational experience. Coverage follows data-sharing partners, and earnings inclusion/attachment rules and suppressed results matter. Do not map a program's graduate earnings to one occupation or claim the institution caused the outcome. [PSEO documentation](https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/pseo_documentation.html), [current API overview](https://www.census.gov/data/developers/data-sets/pseo.html). |
| **Employer and provider pay schedules** | Named employer's service/placement steps, postgraduate training levels, or a particular apprenticeship's pay periods. | The clearest practical evidence for explicit steps when the actual occupation, employer, qualification and stage align. A current schedule is a current example, not a promise that today's student receives those amounts in future calendar years. Examples below. |

No comprehensive current public dataset was established in this review that provides representative Austin salaries after exactly 0/5/10/20 years **in each covered occupation**. Actual labor-market experience, service with one employer, licensed status, job responsibility, age and time since graduation must remain separate variables. Proprietary surveys may ask experience directly, but accepting a model would require its sampling, sample size, occupation/geography mapping and uncertainty documentation; a vendor's percentile-to-experience label would not resolve the gap.

## Practical schedule calibration and a runtime discrepancy

Use a source ledger with employer/provider, occupation/rank, credited experience definition, effective period, actual step, annual contract or hours, base pay, separately stated supplements, review date and source URL. Save those fields per stage. Keep role changes and training transitions explicit. Do not fit a generic occupation curve to one employer and call it a metro average.

- **Austin Police:** public table specifies academy, graduation and anniversaries of graduation. It currently lists $78,627 at graduation, $106,344 at two years, $121,754 at ten and $139,396 at sixteen; top step is at twenty-three. The runtime's choice to carry the two-/sixteen-year values into five-/twenty-year slots is an explicit modeling convention, not a published five-/twenty-year observation. Verify the full governing salary schedule or display the actual source step beside the comparison; do not assume an omitted year has a new raise. [Police pay and benefits](https://www.austintexas.gov/police-recruiting/pay-benefits).
- **Austin ISD:** official compensation page points to the **2026–27 manual**, labels 2025–26 as reference and describes PPfT/incentive additions. Use its current placement and credited-service rules; do not treat a new-hire placement table as a guaranteed path for an incumbent. Exact current manual cells were not reverified here because the linked public Google document exceeded web retrieval limits. [AISD compensation](https://www.austinisd.org/hc/careers/compensation).
- **Dell medical training:** current page, updated September 16, 2026, explicitly labels **2026–27** PGY-1/2/3 at $69,528/$71,747/$74,652 and separately lists 2027–28. These support postgraduate training stages, not qualified physician practice after equivalent years. The first three retained amounts agree. [Dell salary and benefits](https://dellmed.utexas.edu/education/academics/graduate-medical-education/resources/salary-and-benefits).
- **Austin ETA:** table effective January 5, 2026 under the 2025–28 agreement gives first-period $21.07/hour and journeyman $38.30/hour; published annual examples assume forty hours/week. Four-year/8,000-hour training and performance-based advancement do not make six pay periods six years or guarantee full paid hours. This is one program's employee route, not business-owner profit or every Austin electrician's pay. [Austin ETA program](https://austineta.org/apprentice-program-2/).

### Austin Fire saved amount versus current source

The current [official Fire Cadet Employment Overview](https://www.austintexas.gov/fire/fire-cadet-employment), retrieved October 18, 2026, states cadet pay **$22.55/hour / $46,904 annually**, and probationary salary **$67,999 after successful completion of an approximately six-month academy**. It links the 2026 hiring process but supplies no salary effective date or page-update date for that sentence.

The discrepancy affects actual retained runtime code, not only notes:

- `site/dist/salary-progression.js:77` contains `fire?66019:entryAmount`, both for entry and as the floor of later modeled stages.
- `site/dist/salary-progression.js:85` cites the same official Fire URL.
- `site/dist/salary-progression.js:95` labels the example “reviewed October 17, 2026”; line 8 gives the module release as October 16, 2026.
- A read-only call to `salaryProgression('firefighter')` returns **66,019 / 66,019 / 66,019 / 67,726** for entry/5/10/20, marking entry as a published schedule example and later amounts as illustrations. Academy remains **46,904**.
- `site/dist/earnings-evidence.js:2` separately stores the TWC firefighter experienced anchor **67,726**, SOC 33-2011, Austin, 2025 annual wages, with its own TexasWages source. That occupational anchor is distinct from the employer salary; replacing it with $67,999 would conflate sources.

Call this a **saved-versus-current-source discrepancy requiring refresh**, not a proven error on the earlier review date. Before changing amounts, reconcile source date, wage year, rounding and later-stage floors: the currently published employer entry is above the generic experienced anchor, so a truthful scenario may be flat. Do not manufacture increases to make the chart look progressive. No correction was applied in this research task.

## MIT and net-price claims in the synthesis

**MIT claim verified.** Travis County page is updated February 15, 2026 and reports one adult/no children at **$49,279 before tax**, **$42,042 after tax**, **$7,237 taxes**, assuming 2,080 work hours. Prefer the stated annual figure over multiplying the rounded $23.69 hourly display, which differs slightly through rounding. It requests no scraping and links licensing. [County page](https://livingwage.mit.edu/counties/48453).

The methodology confirms basic needs, twelve household types, 2026 estimates standardized to December 2025 dollars, and exclusions for restaurant dining, holidays/vacations and savings/retirement. It includes some civic/entertainment costs, so “no discretionary costs at all” would be too broad. Property/sales taxes are already in cost components; income/payroll taxes are added through a tax model. Avoid adding those taxes twice or treating the model as a quote for a particular household. [MIT methodology](https://livingwage.mit.edu/pages/methodology).

**Net-price claim verified.** UT's current page describes a personalized **2026–27** estimate and defines net price as total attendance cost, including living expenses, **minus grants/scholarships**. It explicitly says the result is nonbinding, based on prior-year costs/aid and not an actual award. Federal Student Aid separately recommends net-price comparison and distinguishing loans/work-study from grant aid. A loan can help finance the remaining price; it does not reduce net price. [UT calculator explanation](https://onestop.utexas.edu/managing-costs/cost-tuition-rates/cost-of-attendance/net-price-calculator/), [FSA aid-offer comparison](https://studentaid.gov/articles/evaluating-financial-aid-offers/).

Keep the student screen brief: “Pay estimate,” employer/area and year, a visible scenario label for generic years and one expandable explanation. The main research already conveys the central limitation accurately. The substantive additions are the exact TWC definitions, discontinued-MWE qualification, real longitudinal-data limitations and the Fire source discrepancy.
